name: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (NeuroStar, BrainsWay Deep TMS, SAINT/SNT)
founders: Mark George / Alvaro Pascual-Leone (rTMS for depression, 1990s)
founded_year_range: TMS 1985; depression rTMS trials 1993-96; NeuroStar FDA clearance Oct 2008; BrainsWay MDD 2013; SAINT 510(k) K220177 cleared 1 Sep 2022
cost_summary: US cash approx. $6,000-15,000 per ~36-session acute course (~$200-500/session; approx., not verified); SAINT reportedly >$20-30k cash (unverified); usually insurance-covered for TRD with copays. Company sites list no prices.
mechanisms: limbic system impairment / amygdala threat conditioning
mechanism_summary: Magnetic induction of cortical currents; repeated trains produce LTP/LTD-like plasticity that propagates through networks. Depression: restore hypoactive left DLPFC and its top-down control over the sgACC/limbic circuit (SAINT targets the DLPFC site most anticorrelated with sgACC on fMRI, using accelerated iTBS). Pain/fibromyalgia: high-frequency M1 stimulation engages descending inhibitory/opioid pathways and restores intracortical inhibition, countering central sensitisation. Each indication has its own target and parameters.
techniques: 10 Hz left DLPFC rTMS, ~36 sessions over 6 weeks
deep TMS H-coil (BrainsWay) with symptom/cue provocation for OCD/smoking
SAINT: fMRI-guided accelerated iTBS, 10 sessions/day x 5 days
high-frequency M1 rTMS for neuropathic pain/fibromyalgia with maintenance sessions
mainstream_notes: Depression: APA (2010) and CANMAT (2016) guidelines, NICE IPG542 (2015), VA and academic centres; FDA-cleared for TRD, anxious depression, adolescent MDD (NeuroStar, 15-21), late-life depression (BrainsWay), OCD and smoking cessation. Pain: IFCN guideline (Lefaucheur 2020) Level A for M1 rTMS in neuropathic pain and Level B for fibromyalgia; weak third-line recommendation (Soliman 2025, Lancet Neurol); Cochrane 2018 rates evidence low/very low quality. Pain use mostly in European specialist centres.
insurance_notes: US commercial insurers, Medicare (LCDs) and Tricare cover treatment-resistant MDD (CPT 90867-90869) after failed antidepressant trials and prior authorisation; OCD coverage is growing; pain and fibromyalgia are generally not covered in the US. SAINT-specific reimbursement not verified.

key_trials.citation: O'Reardon JP et al. Biol Psychiatry 2007;62:1208-16 (PMID 17573044)
key_trials.design: Multisite double-blind sham-controlled RCT, NeuroStar pivotal (industry)
key_trials.finding: Active TMS superior to sham on MADRS at week 4 (with post hoc baseline-severity correction) and on HAMD at weeks 4 and 6; remission ~2x sham

key_trials.citation: George MS et al. Arch Gen Psychiatry 2010;67:507-16 (PMID 20439832)
Levkovitz Y et al. World Psychiatry 2015;14:64-73 (PMID 25655160)
key_trials.design: Multicenter sham-controlled RCT of deep TMS (BrainsWay H-coil)
key_trials.finding: Response 38.4% vs 21.4%; remission 32.6% vs 14.6% at week 5; sustained through the 12-week maintenance phase

key_trials.design: Randomised non-inferiority trial, iTBS vs 10 Hz rTMS
key_trials.finding: 3-min iTBS non-inferior to 37-min 10 Hz rTMS for TRD

key_trials.citation: Yesavage JA et al. JAMA Psychiatry 2018;75:884-893 (PMID 29955803)
key_trials.design: VA Cooperative Studies double-blind sham-controlled RCT, 9 VA centres
key_trials.finding: No significant difference in remission between active 10 Hz left DLPFC rTMS and sham (~41% vs ~37%); important independent null result

key_trials.citation: Cole EJ et al. Am J Psychiatry 2020;177:716-726 (PMID 32252538)
key_trials.finding: Remission in 19/21 with outcome data (90.5%) after 5 days; 86.4% of 22 by ITT

key_trials.citation: Cole EJ et al. Am J Psychiatry 2022;179:132-141 (PMID 34711062)
key_trials.design: Double-blind sham RCT of SNT/SAINT, planned interim analysis (32 enrolled; 14 active, 15 sham)
key_trials.finding: MADRS reduction 52.5% active vs 11.1% sham at 4 weeks post-treatment

key_trials.design: Sham-controlled RCT, M1 rTMS in fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Reduced widespread pain from the 5th session, lasting ~2 weeks after treatment

key_trials.design: Sham-controlled RCT with maintenance, fibromyalgia (30 completers)
key_trials.finding: Pain reduction maintained to week 25; correlated with intracortical inhibition changes

key_trials.design: Multicentre sham-controlled RCT, neuronavigated M1 vs DLPFC rTMS, peripheral neuropathic pain
key_trials.finding: M1 rTMS reduced pain vs sham over 25 weeks; DLPFC did not

key_trials.citation: Silva VA et al. Br J Anaesth 2025;134:1756-64 (PMID 40087077)
key_trials.design: Multicentre sham-controlled RCT, add-on M1 rTMS in fibromyalgia (women; Brazil, France, Japan)
key_trials.finding: Week-8 50% responder OR 3.04, NNT ~4.5; relative pain reduction 40.4% vs 18.4%; analgesia waned by week 16, FIQ gains persisted

key_trials.citation: Toh EYJ et al. Psychosom Med 2022;84:400-409 (PMID 35100184)
key_trials.finding: Pain SMD -0.35, QoL SMD -0.51 vs sham; no effect on depression/anxiety; M1 drove pain benefit (SMD -0.57)

key_trials.citation: O'Connell NE et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2018;CD008208 (PMID 29547226)
key_trials.design: Cochrane systematic review of non-invasive brain stimulation for chronic pain (rTMS: 27 studies in short-term pain meta-analysis)
key_trials.finding: rTMS vs sham small short-term effect (SMD -0.22, ~7% pain reduction), low-quality evidence; no evidence for low-frequency or DLPFC rTMS

key_trials.citation: Soliman N et al. Lancet Neurol 2025;24:413-428 (PMID 40252663)
key_trials.design: NeuPSIG systematic review/meta-analysis of neuropathic pain treatments (313 RCTs, 29 neuromodulation)
key_trials.finding: rTMS NNT 4.2 (95% CI 2.3-28.3; low certainty); weak third-line recommendation

controversy: Moderate effect sizes against sham; imperfect sham blinding and industry-sponsored pivotal trials (NeuroStar week-4 MADRS result needed post hoc baseline correction); a large independent VA RCT (Yesavage 2018, N=164) found no active-sham difference. Expectancy effects from intensive daily clinic contact. SAINT's ~90% remission figure is open-label; its RCT was small and reported at interim. NeuroStar's '62% remission' is uncontrolled registry CGI-S data. Cochrane rates chronic-pain evidence low/very low quality. High cost and limited access. Off-label clinic marketing (anxiety, autism, long COVID). Pain benefits fade without maintenance. Rare seizures.

indicators.value: NeuroStar 2008; BrainsWay MDD 2013, OCD 2018, smoking 2020; SAINT K220177 cleared 1 Sep 2022
Major US insurers began covering TRD ~2011-2013; now most plans incl. Medicare

popularity.reach_estimate: ~1-2 million people worldwide cumulatively (estimate; NeuroStar alone >250k verified; plus BrainsWay, Magstim/MagVenture and other systems, and Canadian/European/Asian use)
popularity.method_notes: The trajectory is anchored to regulatory milestones (FDA 2008/2013/2018/2020/2022), the spread of insurance coverage (2011-2013), publication growth, the 2020-22 SAINT media spike, and company-reported cumulative patients (NeuroStar >250k, verified on site). Reach and trajectory are partly estimated from background knowledge. Google Trends and Reddit member counts were not verified numerically. An unverified '~19 fibromyalgia RCTs' indicator was removed during fact-checking.
